Mistborn was alright. It's a bit of a slog through some of it.

His idea of a magic system is fairly interesting in how it works, but doesn't seem realistic in any way. You have to suspend belief from the very beginning in a pretty big way. That's not a big deal, but versus a lot of fantasy, it's a fairly big burden. This isn't a dig necessarily, just a deviation from what most fantasy is, low-magic.

I don't enjoy the backstory of how the world was changed by the Emperor and once they figure him and his backstory out, the whole thing seems to go a little downhill for me, although I really enjoyed it up to that point.

There's too much character introspection. All of the main characters seem to share the character trait in which they doubt themselves a lot and spend a lot of time dwelling on that. There's a bit too much of that in there for me I think as well.

The later books have too many metal combinations that aren't useful except for that one story plot (I'm not alluding to a specific plot, I mean in general). The combination is discovered, used at precisely the right time, and then barely mentioned or used ever again. It gets a little ridiculous.

The ending was terrible.

Funny I really liked the ending. The reason why I liked it is because you could see it coming. It wasn't like one of those mysteries where the detective has everyone in a room at the end for the reveal and you say to yourself, "bullshit there were not enough clues to figure this out". You actually can figure it out before it happens.
